3. The plaintiff's case, in short, is that one Pitambar Gope was the original owner in possession of Schedule 1(ka) land in rayati right and under him one Nida Gazi was in possession in korfa right in khatian No. 42. Before the last settlement operation the said Pitambar transferred the land of Schedule 1 (Ka) to Guru Das Dhupi and his brothers and during settlement operation the land was recorded in the names of the said purchasers. The aforesaid Pitambar died leaving his sons, Rajani Kanta Cope and Ramani Kanta Gope as his heirs in respect of the first Schedule land. Subsequently the rent in respect of first Schedule land became arrear and the landlord Chandi Charan Laha filed Rent Suit No. 3552 of 1931 in the court of Munsif, Comilla and obtained a decree and put the decree in execution in Rent Execution Case No. 3227 of 1934 and the said landlord auction purchased 15.98 acres of land and the sale was confirmed on 2-1-35 and the landlord also took delivery of possession therein through court. Thereafter the said Chandi Charan died leaving behind his sons Tarini Chandra Laha and others as heirs and by virtue of an amicable partition between the brothers, the first Schedule land fell exclusively in the saham of Tarini Chandra Laha. Due to the aforesaid auction sale, the korfa interest of Nida Gazi ceased to exist. The aforesaid Nida Gazi died leaving behind his mother, Johara, brothers, defendant No.1-3 and sister defendant No. 4. Thereafter the said Johara Gazi took settlement of 0.4 acre out of 0.19 acres of plot No. 54, .39 acres of plot No. 377, 0.10 acres of plot No. 384, 1.23 acres out of plot No.391, 0.27 acres of plot No. 392 and western .04 acres of plot No. 393 ie in all 2.43 acres at an annual rental of Taka 18 in the month of April, 1940. Thereafter the said Johara Bibi died leaving behind the defendant Nos. 1-4 as heirs. 

 4. The said Tarini Chandra granted settlement of 3.72 acres of land of various plots of khatian Nos. 41 and 42 to one Ruhini Lal Das by a registered kabuliyat dated 3-9-42. The said Tarini Chandra granted settlement of 4.51 acres of land of khatian No. 41 to one Durga Chandra Das and Shyama Chandra Das by a registered kabuliat dated 2-10-42. Thereafter Durga Chandra died leaving behind plaintiff No.3 and Shyama Charan died leaving behind plaintiff Nos.1 and 2 who had been possessing the same. The said Tarini Chandra granted rayati settlement of 2.43 acres of khatian No. 41 to one Bharat Chandra Das by a registered kabuliat dated 1-4-43 and delivered possession. Thereafter the said Tarini Chandra granted settlement of 1.46½ acres of land of khatian No. 41 to Mohini and Jagat, brothers of Bharat Chandra. The said Mohini Chandra died childless leaving behind her brothers, Jagat Chandra and Bharat Chandra who became the owners of his property. Jagat Chandra died leaving his only daughter Haribala and Bharat Chandra died leaving his only daughter Hemlata who became the owners in possession of the property left by their respective father. The aforesaid Tarini Chandra out of Schedule I land granted settlement of 0.65 acres of plot No. 16 and 32½ acres of plot No. 481 to Copal Chandra Das and also 0.77 acres of plot No. 464 to Abhoy Chandra Das on the basis of kabuliat. Thus Tarini Chandra ceased to have any interest in Schedule I land. 

 5. The lands taken settlement by Jahora Bibi was recorded in RS Khatian No. 46 but due to mistake 2.43 acres was recorded in place of 2.65 acres. Thus the said record of right was wrong and the defendant Nos.1-4 have no title or interest therein. The said lands are in possession of the plaintiffs. The lands of Rohini Das was correctly recorded in RS Khatian No. 98 who sold .44 acres land of plot No.543 of khatian No. 42 of Schedule 1(Ka) to Osman Ali by a registered kabala on 4-3-68. Thereafter the said Rohini sold .64 acres of plot No. 562 of Khatian No. 42 of Schedule 1(Ka) to Azimunnessa and her son Muslimuddin by a registered kabala dated 14-3-70. In RS Khatian No.97 an area of 4.15 acres of land settlement by Durga Charan and Symacharan was recorded in their names. In the said khatian in plot No. 393 an area of 1.07 acres of land belonging to the plaintiff has not been at all recorded and the plaintiffs being the owner are in possession of the same. 

 6. As the suit land of Schedule II has been wrongly recorded in the name of defendant's predecessor Johura Bibi in RS Khatian No. 46, the defendants falsely raised claim over the land and as such, cloud has been cast upon their title. It transpired that the defendants collusively created two mutation khatians in respect of plot No. 393. The plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land from the time of their predecessor for long over 12 years and subsequently the defendants illegally trespassed into the suit land on 24th Sraban, 1389 BS and thereby dispossessed the plaintiffs. 

 8. Their further case is that, Pitambar Cope was the owner in possession of Schedule 1(Ka) and belonging to khatian No. 41 and that in khatian No. 42 within the said khatian lands measuring 6.07 was taken korfa settlement by Nida Gazi by a registered kabuliat dated 20-11-17 and was paying rent regularly. There was never any rent suit, rent decree or auction sale as alleged in the plaint and all these are mere paper transactions. There was never any delivery of possession through court. The interest of Nida Gazi was not affected by the auction sale and Nida Gazi was never evicted from the lands of Khatian No. 42. The plaintiffs case of granting settlement by Tarini Chandra in favour of several persons by kabuliat are all false and collusive. The defendants are in possession of 1.47 acres of land in plot No. 393 described in Schedule II by inheritance. Taking advantage of the minority of defendants and old age of their mother Johara Bibi the plaintiffs predecessor Durga Charan in collusion with settlement staff got the lands belonging to and in possession of the plaintiffs in respect of plot Nos. 49/50/393/391/54/481 of Khatin No. 97 recorded in the names of Durga Charan and Shyma Charan. The said khatian is wrong and Johura Gazi never took any settlement of the lands of Khatian No. 42 and she was possessing the same by inheritance and on her death the defendants are possessing the same. The plaintiffs had never any title or possession in the suit land. The defendants are illiterate and the plaintiffs with ulterior motive created RS Khatian No. 98 in respect of the land of Khatian No. 42 and the defendants are not aware of any mutation of their names in respect of Khatian No. 97 which was collusively created by the plaintiffs. Their further case is that the plaintiffs falsely alleged that the defendants dispossessed them from the suit land on 24th Sraban, 1389 BS. The defendants did not dispossess the plaintiffs on the said date. The defendants instituted Tile Suit No. 16 of 1983 in respect of the suit land alleging wrong recording of the RS Khatian which is pending. 

 14. Mr Syed Mahmud Hussain, the learned Advocate for the opposite parties submits that the land of Khatian No.42 measuring 6.07 acres of land belonged to Nida Gazi in korfa right and after his death his heirs the defendants have been in possession. He further submits that there was no Rent sale and the land of Khatian No. 42 was never sold in auction. He further submits that the plaintiffs case is that the land of Khatian No. 41 was sold in auction but no delivery of possession was taken through court in respect of the land sold in auction as claimed by the plaintiffs-petitioners. He further submits that in the sale certificate filed by the plaintiffs the suit plot No.393 does not find place. He further submits that no writ of delivery of possession has been filed in support of the plaintiffs contention that after auction purchase the landlord took delivery of possession through court. From the certified copy of suit register also it appears that no delivery of possession was taken through court after the alleged auction purchase. He also submits that as per law after auction purchase korfa tenancy of Nida Gazi which was an encumbrance was to be annulled under provision of section 167 of the Bengal Tenancy Act. But there was no such annulment. 

 15. Exhibit No.1, CS Khatian No.41 of Mouja-Bhowri, PS Chandina, District-Comilla shows that an area of 9.91 acres of land in 13 plots was recorded in the name of one Pitambar Cope under landlord Rajakunga Das Laha and others and under Khatian No.41 in Khatian No.42 an area of 6.07 acres of land in 12 plots was recorded in the name of Nida Gazi in Korfa right. CS Khatian No.41 shows that all the 13 plots recorded in the Khatian were sold out before or at least during CS operation by the recorded tenant to different persons and accordingly in all the 13 plots of land of Khatian No.41 the possession of the purchasers was recorded and this position is not disputed. 

 16. Plaintiffs-petitioners case is that landlord Chandi Charan Laha brought Rent Suit No.3752 of 1931 in the Court of Munsif, Comilla against Pitambar and obtained a decree, put the decree into execution in Rent Execution case No.3227 of 1934 and the landlord auction purchased 15.98 acres of land and the sale was confirmed and they took delivery of possession through Court. The defendant's case, on the other hand, is that there was no such Rent Suit and no auction purchase by the landlord and no delivery of possession was taken through court. Their further case is that the land of Khatian No. 42 which Nida Gazi possessed in korfa right was not sold in auction as Nida Gazi was not a tenant under Laha Babus. From the certified copy of sale certificate it appears that the suit plot No. 393 does not find place in the sale certificate. So it cannot be said that plot No. 393 was also sold in auction as claimed by the plaintiffs. No writ of delivery of possession was filed to show that after auction purchase, the landlord took delivery of possession through court. The certified copy of Rent suit Register Ext.6 shows that there is no note in the Register regarding taking delivery of possession in the land. There is also no evidence on record to show that the korfa tenancy of Nida Gazi was annulled as per provision of section 167 of the Bengal Tenancy Act after the alleged auction purchase by the landlord. 

 17. Mr BK Das submits that Nida Gazi took korfa settlement of the lands of Khatian No. 42 for a period of 5 years and after the expiry of the period of 5 years the korfa tenancy of Nida Gazi extinguished and as such there was no necessity for annulment of the encumbrance after auction purchase by the landlord. In reply Mr Hussain, the learned Advocate for the opposite parties submits that from the evidence of PW 1 Rai Horon Banik and PW 2 Md Jafar Ali it is clear that the korfa settlement of Nida Gazi continued till the date of alleged auction sale. PW 2 further stated that the landlord took delivery of possession in the suit land by demolishing the dwelling huts of the defendant ie the heirs of Nida Gazi. From this it is clear that Nida Gazi and after him, his heirs were in possession of the land of Khatian No. 42 after the expiry of the initial period of 5 years. So the contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioners that after the expiry of 5 years the korfa tenancy of Nida Gazi ceased to exist does not stand. The learned Advocate for the opposite parties in support of his contention placed the case of Jagabandu Basak and others vs. Karim Mondal and others, reported in 8 DLR 366. In that case it was held that, if an under raiyat has been allowed to continue in occupation, his tenancy can only be terminated in accordance with the provision of the Bengal Tenancy Act. Until such steps have been taken in time he cannot be ejected from his land. In the instant case there was no case of the plaintiff-petitioners in the plaint that after expiry of the period of 5 years the korfa tenancy of Nida Gazi ceased to exist. Thus from the evidence on record it is proved that the korfa tenancy of Nida Gazi continued after the expiry of 5 years for which initially Nida Gazi took korfa settlement of the land of Khatian No. 42 and after Nida Gazi his heirs continued to possess. 

 19. Mr Hussain next submits that under section 160(c) of the Bengal Tenancy Act the under tenancy of Nida Gazi is protected for as per CS Khatian No. 42 there are homestead, tank, etc. in the land. So, the landlord was entitled to claim enhancement of rent only if the auction purchase by the landlord is proved. CS Khatina No. 42 shows that plot No. 391 is homestead and plot Nos. 54, 377, 384 are tanks. Sub-section (c) of section 160 of the Bengal Tenancy Act provides that, "(c) any lease of land whereon dwelling houses, manufactories or other permanent buildings have been erected, or permanent gardens, plantations, tanks, canals, places of worship or burning or burying grounds have been made shall be deemed to be protected interest." 

 24. Mr BK Das next submits that the plaintiff-petitioners filed an application on 22-7-91 before the learned District Judge under Order 41 rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure with annexure of registered deed of partition dated 1-5-41 praying for accepting the same as additional evidence for the purpose of showing that Chandi Charan was the superior landlord of the suit land and the application was fixed for hearing on 2-10-91. But ultimately, the appeal was disposed of without deciding the said application and this has caused prejudice to the plaintiffs. It is not disputed that Chandi Charan was the landlord in respect of Khatian No.41. The copy of deed of partition dated 1-5-41 was filed to show that by the amicable partition Tarini got the land of Khatian No.41 in his share and thereafter he settled the land to different persons including the plaintiffs. It is not disputed that Laha Babus were landlords in respect of CS Khatian No. 41. So, in my poinion, the non-consideration of this document by the court of appeal below did not cause any prejudice to the plaintiffs-petitioners.
